title: Mitigation of harmful algal blooms caused by Alexandrium catenella and reduction in saxitoxin accumulation in bivalves using cultivable seaweeds
organism: Saccharina latissima, Ulva, Chondrus → Alexandrium catenella
scale: 250 mL flasks; field bottles; 300 L mesocosm
result: -17-74% at 2-3 d and -42-96% at ~1 wk; in 300 L mesocosms kelp -73% in 48 h and Ulva -54% in 96 h.
env_effects: Mesocosm total chlorophyll did not fall (other algae replaced the target); Ulva pushed pH to 9.0-9.5 (sometimes >10), kelp stayed 8.1-8.9; mussel STX 71.8 vs 93.5 µg/100 g.

title: Cultivable seaweeds eliminate the lethal effects of the harmful alga, Margalefidinium polykrikoides, on early life stage fish
organism: Ulva, Gracilaria, Chondrus, Grateloupia → Margalefidinium polykrikoides; larval fish
result: No cell reduction until day 5, then -68%, -90% and -92% on days 5-7; fish survival extended, with protection needing close contact.
env_effects: DMSP alone reduced toxicity to fish; live seaweed beat frozen.

title: Inhibition of cosmopolitan toxic diatom, Pseudo‐nitzschia, by seaweeds
organism: kelp, Ulva, Gracilaria → Pseudo-nitzschia (diatom)
result: -13-47% at 24-48 h and -74-94% at ≥72 h; bloom water kelp 2 g/L -69 to -81%, 1 g/L n.s.; Gracilaria no effect.
env_effects: Diatoms lost photosynthetic efficiency and paled.

title: The green macroalga, Ulva lactuca, inhibits the growth of seven common harmful algal bloom species via allelopathy
organism: Ulva lactuca → 7 HAB species
result: -24% (P. minimum), -38% (Karlodinium), -50% (K. brevis) at 72 h; extracts lysed Karlodinium and K. brevis after 5 d.
env_effects: Heat-stable allelochemicals.

title: Comparative studies on the allelopathic effects of two different strains of Ulva pertusa on Heterosigma akashiwo and Alexandrium tamarense
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
organism: Ulva pertusa (2 strains) → Heterosigma akashiwo, Alexandrium tamarense
scale: 100 mL flasks with 40 mL f/2; axenic cultures; triplicate
dose: fresh tissue 0.625-10 g-wet/L; dry powder 0.15-2.4 g-dry/L; isolation co-culture 2.5 g-wet/L
duration: 10 d coexistence; short-term lysis assays in hours
result: Fresh-tissue EC50 0.3 (nonsexual) / 0.6 (sexual strain) g-wet/L for H. akashiwo and 2.0 / 2.5 g-wet/L for A. tamarense; 5-10 g-wet/L killed all H. akashiwo within 2 days, but A. tamarense was never killed. Culture filtrate did not significantly inhibit either species.
env_effects: Not reported.
key_details: Axenic lab co-cultures of two Ulva pertusa strains (sexual and nonsexual) with H. akashiwo or A. tamarense in 40 mL f/2, n=3, t-tests; nutrients topped up to rule out competition. H. akashiwo growth was lowered at all fresh-tissue doses and all cells died within 2 d at 5 and 10 g-wet/L; A. tamarense was inhibited only above 1.25 g-wet/L with no lethal effect even at 10 g-wet/L. Dry powder EC50s were 0.4/1.0 g-dry/L (H. akashiwo) and 0.6/0.8 g-dry/L (A. tamarense); low powder doses sometimes stimulated growth (H. akashiwo at 0.6 g-dry/L sexual strain; A. tamarense day 6-7 at 0.15 g-dry/L), and survivors revived after day 4-6. Filtrate (initial or semi-continuous) had no significant effect, while physically separated (isolation) co-culture at 2.5 g-wet/L still killed H. akashiwo, suggesting labile allelochemicals needing continuous release. Lysis LT50 for H. akashiwo was 3.0-7.0 h.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record lists only the A. tamarense EC50; the much lower H. akashiwo EC50 (0.3-0.6 g-wet/L) and complete kill of H. akashiwo at 5-10 g-wet/L were missing. Low powder doses could stimulate growth.

title: Allelopathic interactions between the macroalga Ulva pertusa and eight microalgal species
organism: Ulva pertusa → 8 microalgae incl. Skeletonema, Nitzschia, Chaetoceros, A. tamarense
scale: 100 mL flasks with 40 mL f/2; axenic; triplicate batch, nutrient-replete semi-continuous and isolated co-cultures
dose: 12.5 g-wet/L fresh U. pertusa; filtrate from 80 g-wet/L
result: Batch co-culture killed H. akashiwo and S. costatum (100%) and cut the other six species 42-84% (A. tamarense 70%); in nutrient-replete semi-continuous culture reductions were 28-90% (A. tamarense 52%). Culture filtrate inhibited only Chroomonas placoidea.
env_effects: Nutrient-replete cultures (NO3 >= 780 umol/L, PO4 >= 36 umol/L) still showed inhibition, ruling out nutrient competition; pH 8.7 +/- 0.3. Some microalgae reduced Ulva growth by 20-30%.
key_details: Axenic lab study: Ulva pertusa (12.5 g-wet/L) co-cultured with eight microalgae in batch, nutrient-replete semi-continuous, and isolated (separated) co-cultures, n=3 each. Percent growth reduction at end (batch/semi-continuous/isolated): H. akashiwo and S. costatum 100/100/100; A. tamarense 70/52/56; Nitzschia 59/28/21; Chaetoceros 42/70/74; Isochrysis 84/90/88; Chroomonas 76/60/67; Tetraselmis 63/60/56. Filtrate (80 g-wet/L, 3 d) inhibited only Chroomonas, so continuous contact/release is needed. Microalgae in turn changed Ulva growth (+16% with H. akashiwo, -20 to -30% with Tetraselmis, Nitzschia, Chaetoceros).
fulltext_discrepancy: Record said per-species diatom numbers were not retrieved; full table gives them (Skeletonema 100%, Nitzschia 59%, Chaetoceros 42% in batch). The ~70% A. tamarense figure is the batch value; semi-continuous nutrient-replete value is 52%.

title: Allelopathic growth inhibition of Prorocentrum micans (Dinophyta) by Ulva pertusa and Ulva linza (Chlorophyta) in laboratory cultures
organism: Ulva pertusa, U. linza → Prorocentrum micans
result: Fresh Ulva tissue above 0.625 g/L and dry powder above 0.15 g/L significantly cut P. micans growth; 10 g/L fresh tissue and 2.4 g/L powder killed the cultures (EC50 fresh 1.8 and 2.3 g/L; powder 0.7 and 0.8 g/L). Aqueous and methanol extracts inhibited, other solvents did not; a single filtrate dose had no effect but semi-continuous addition did.
env_effects: P. micans did not affect the seaweed; active compounds polar.
key_details: Lab flasks in f/2 at 20°C with an axenic P. micans strain and antibiotic-treated Ulva collected during a Qingdao bloom (May 2003); n = 4 replicates per treatment with untreated controls. Fresh-tissue doses 0.625-10 g/L and powder 0.15-2.4 g/L; at 2.4 g/L powder cultures died completely within 4 days. Methanol extract EC50 was 0.015 ppt (U. pertusa) and 0.017 ppt (U. linza); aqueous extract inhibited above 0.1 ppt over 6 d. P. micans had no effect on Ulva growth in 20-day co-culture. Doses are high (grams of seaweed per litre) relative to open water.

title: Effects of macroalgae Ulva pertusa (Chlorophyta) and Gracilaria lemaneiformis (Rhodophyta) on growth of four species of bloom-forming dinoflagellates
organism: Ulva pertusa, Gracilaria lemaneiformis → 4 dinoflagellates
scale: 250 mL flasks, 150 mL f/2-enriched seawater; n=3
result: U. pertusa thalli killed all P. donghaiense, S. trochoidea and A. tamarense within 144 h (LT50 37.9, 63.6, 59.8 h) and cut A. carterae 34%; G. lemaneiformis killed P. donghaiense (LT50 138.6 h) and cut S. trochoidea 79%, A. tamarense 24%, A. carterae 20%.
env_effects: Filtrates were inconsistent: U. pertusa filtrate stimulated A. carterae +78% and G. lemaneiformis filtrate stimulated A. tamarense +33%. G. lemaneiformis exhausted N and P (3.6 and 0.32 umol/L left), so its effect was partly nutrient competition (relieved by daily f/2); U. pertusa left N and P well above limiting.
key_details: Lab batch co-cultures (n=3, one-way ANOVA) of fresh U. pertusa or G. lemaneiformis thalli (0.5 g FW in 150 mL) with four dinoflagellates at 1.0x10^4 cells/mL (A. tamarense 0.4x10^4). U. pertusa was algicidal to three species (all cells dead within 144 h); G. lemaneiformis was lethal only to P. donghaiense. Culture filtrates gave species-specific inhibition or stimulation (Table 1). Nutrient tests showed G. lemaneiformis' effect on P. donghaiense was largely nutrient depletion (alleviated by daily f/2), while NaHCO3 addition did not relieve U. pertusa inhibition, pointing to allelopathy.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record's G. lemaneiformis results and its nutrient-competition caveat were missing; 'filtrate inhibited 5-27%' refers only to U. pertusa filtrate on three species. The stimulation of A. carterae (+78%) was by U. pertusa filtrate, not a general filtrate effect.

title: Allelopathic effects of Ulva lactuca on selected species of harmful bloom-forming microalgae in laboratory cultures
organism: Ulva lactuca → HAB microalgae
result: -48% A. tamarense; filtrate inhibited only for the first 2 d, then growth recovered; powder EC50 0.19 g/L DW (3 d).
env_effects: Not reported.

title: Algicidal activity of polyunsaturated fatty acids derived from Ulva fasciata and U. pertusa (Ulvaceae, Chlorophyta) on phytoplankton
organism: Ulva fasciata, U. pertusa → 10+ red-tide species
dose: powder 1.5 g/L DW; fresh tissue 50 g/L
result: Powder 4 h LC50 0.40-0.70 g/L DW against Heterosigma; fresh tissue at 50 g/L killed only 1.6-6.6% in 4 h; PUFAs 2% of peak left at 48 h.
env_effects: Not reported.

title: Effects of two species of macroalgae—Ulva pertusa and Gracilaria lemaneiformis—on growth of Heterosigma akashiwo (Raphidophyceae)
organism: Ulva pertusa, Gracilaria lemaneiformis → Heterosigma akashiwo
dose: fresh thalli 0.34-3.4 g FW/L; filtrate from 4-40 g FW/L; water-soluble extract 0.5-4.0 mL; dry powder
result: U. pertusa fresh thalli, extract and powder (3.4 g/L) killed all H. akashiwo within 120 h (LT50 45.9, 71.7, 66.7 h); fresh thalli killed all cells at >=0.68 g FW/L but only cut numbers ~53% at 0.34 g FW/L. G. lemaneiformis thalli killed all cells at 3.4 g/L (LT50 132.1 h) but stimulated growth ~56% at 0.34 g/L.
env_effects: Ulva co-culture left NO3 470 and PO4 177.2 umol/L (not limiting); Gracilaria exhausted them to ~11.2 and 4.35 umol/L, and daily f/2 relieved its inhibition. Low doses stimulated H. akashiwo: 0.5 mL Ulva extract +72%, 0.34 g/L Gracilaria +56%, Gracilaria dry powder increased growth.
key_details: Lab co-cultures (n=3, ANOVA) of H. akashiwo (1-25x10^4 cells/mL) with fresh thalli, culture filtrate, water-soluble extract or dry powder of U. pertusa or G. lemaneiformis over 72-216 h. U. pertusa was strongly algicidal and dose-dependent (LT50 83.0, 57.9, 35.9 h at 0.68, 1.7, 3.4 g FW/L); filtrate from 40 g/L killed cells within 72 h but filtrates from 4-20 g/L acted only after 72 h, and 3.4 g/L filtrate cut cells to ~52% of control by 216 h. G. lemaneiformis acted mostly via nutrient depletion. Low doses of both algae stimulated the target (hormesis).
fulltext_discrepancy: Record had duration 'Not reported' (72-216 h) and no doses; it omitted that low doses stimulated H. akashiwo (+56% to +72%) and that Ulva needs >=0.68 g FW/L for complete kill.

title: The ability of the red macroalga, Porphyra purpurea (Rhodophyceae) to inhibit the proliferation of seven common harmful microalgae
organism: Porphyra purpurea → 7 HAB species
scale: lab cultures (n=3); 48 h field bottle incubations with Long Island brown-tide water; larval fish bioassay
dose: fresh thalli 20 and 180 mg dry wt/L (P. multiseries 80 and 320); field 1.0 and 9.0 mg dry wt/L; extracts equivalent to 180 mg dry wt/L
duration: 120 h lab (72 h for P. multiseries); 48 h field
result: At 180 mg dry wt/L fresh P. purpurea cut A. anophagefferens >97% (also at 20 mg/L), C. marina 64%, P. multiseries 63%, K. veneficum 49%, K. brevis 44%, C. polykrikoides 30%, P. minimum 20% over 5 d. In natural brown-tide water 9.0 mg dry wt/L cut A. anophagefferens only 21-44% in 48 h (13-28% in 2010).
env_effects: No mortality or abnormal behaviour in 1-week-old sheepshead minnows over 120 h at 900 mg dry wt/L thalli or 180 mg/L extract. Residual nitrate >1,000 uM and phosphate >70 uM, so inhibition was not nutrient limitation.
key_details: Lab co-cultures (triplicate, two-way ANOVA) of fresh Porphyra purpurea thalli at two doses with seven HAB species for 5 d; inhibition was dose- and time-dependent with a synergistic interaction. Sensitivity order: A. anophagefferens > C. marina > K. veneficum > P. multiseries > K. brevis > C. polykrikoides > P. minimum. Extract of fresh thalli (180 mg dry wt/L equivalent) completely eliminated growth of A. anophagefferens, K. brevis, K. veneficum and C. polykrikoides and was more potent than extract of dried powder. P. purpurea was more potent than Ulva lactuca against A. anophagefferens and similar for five other species. Three 48 h field incubations with brown-tide water gave modest reductions (13-44%) only at the higher dose; nutrient addition had no effect.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record dose was a placeholder ('mg/L') and duration 'Not reported'; actual doses 20-180 mg dry wt/L and 5 d. Record said extracts of fresh or dried tissue were 'equal or stronger' than thalli; full text shows fresh-thallus extract was clearly more potent than dried-powder extract. Field-water effect (13-44%) was much weaker than lab effect.

title: Inhibition of marine coastal bloom-forming phytoplankton by commercially cultivated Gracilaria lemaneiformis (Rhodophyta)
organism: Gracilaria lemaneiformis -> Dunaliella salina, Prorocentrum micans, Skeletonema costatum, Scrippsiella trochoidea, Chaetoceros curvisetus, Platymonas subcordiformis, natural assemblage incl. Phaeocystis globosa
scale: 40 mL lab; 1 L in situ bottles (Zhuhai); 50 L and 1000 L mesocosms (Nan'ao Island); field survey 2010 and 2012
dose: lab 1.25-25 g FW/L; bottles 10 and 40 g/L; 50 L mesocosm 1.0-6.0 g wet wt/L; 1000 L mesocosm 3 and 6 kg (3.0 and 6.0 g wet wt/L)
duration: lab ~7 d; bottles 3 d; mesocosms 10 d
result: In lab, >1.25 g/L inhibited 4 of 6 species and >12.5 g/L stopped growth completely; bloom-water bottles with P. globosa fell 75-88% vs control in 3 d, 50 L mesocosms 70-82% by day 8, and the 1000 L mesocosm Skeletonema bloom peak was about an order of magnitude lower (3.78x10^6 and 1.33x10^6 vs 3.88x10^7 cells/L).
env_effects: In the 1000 L mesocosm phytoplankton in treatments exceeded control by day 10 after the control bloom crashed; species richness was higher with Gracilaria. Field: phytoplankton abundance lower in farmed areas before harvest; difference vanished after harvest (correlational).
key_details: Multi-scale study, all at least triplicate. Lab: G. lemaneiformis (0-25 g FW/L) significantly inhibited D. salina, P. micans, S. costatum and S. trochoidea above 1.25 g/L, with no effect on C. curvisetus or P. subcordiformis; a natural assemblage died within 2 days above 12.5 g/L. In situ 1 L bottles with P. globosa bloom water (~30x10^3 cells/mL): 22-38% inhibition at 1 d rising to 75-88% at 3 d at 10-40 g/L. 50 L mesocosm: 1-6 g wet wt/L all inhibited, gap growing from <20% (day 2) to 70-82% (day 8). 1000 L mesocosm: bloom peak one order of magnitude lower, but treatments overtook control after day 8. Field 2012: significantly lower abundance in cultivation area before harvest, no difference after harvest (t-tests, 3 vs 3 stations).
fulltext_discrepancy: Record species list was partly wrong (no Phaeocystis in lab tests; lab species were D. salina, P. micans, S. costatum, S. trochoidea, C. curvisetus, P. subcordiformis) and setting labelled 'field' though core evidence is lab and mesocosm. Quantitative mesocosm results (70-88% reduction) were missing; 1000 L treatments exceeded control at day 10.

title: Allelopathic interactions between the HAB dinoflagellate Ostreopsis cf. ovata and macroalgae
organism: Ulva rigida, Dictyota, Rhodymenia → Ostreopsis cf. ovata
result: Ulva co-culture ended 94% below the inoculum (LT50 12 d); powder -17-37%; filtrate stimulated growth.
env_effects: Ulva drew down DIN, PO4 unchanged; target cells formed cysts.

title: New insights on the species-specific allelopathic interactions between macrophytes and marine HAB dinoflagellates
organism: Ulva rigida, 2 seagrasses → Ostreopsis, Prorocentrum lima, Coolia, Alexandrium pacificum
result: Growth rates -35-62% in benthic species; A. pacificum all dead by day 6 at ≥0.8 g/L (EC50 <0.4 g/L FW); Fv/Fm fell 13-15%.
env_effects: pH, DO and nutrients not different from controls.

title: Inhibition of harmful algal blooms caused by Aureococcus anophagefferens (Pelagophyceae) using native (Gracilaria tikvahiae) and invasive (Dasysiphonia japonica) red seaweeds from North America
organism: Gracilaria tikvahiae, Dasysiphonia → Aureococcus
result: Dose-dependent reductions in nearly all lab runs, needing ≥0.75-1 g/L and ≥72 h at low nutrients; field bottles 24 h: Dasysiphonia 3 g/L -30%, Gracilaria n.s.
env_effects: pH 9.0 alone inhibited Aureococcus; pH 8.00-8.50 did not.

title: Mechanism of the allelopathic effect of macroalgae Gracilaria bailiniae on Nitzschia closterium
organism: Gracilaria bailiniae → Nitzschia closterium (fouling benthic diatom)
scale: Lab flask co-cultures, n = 3 replicates per concentration
dose: Four concentrations each of fresh thalli (GFT) and aqueous extract (GAE); allelochemicals citrate, hydroxyethanesulfonic (isethionic) acid, taurine
result: Fresh thalli suppressed N. closterium at all concentrations by day 4 (IC50-4d 0.667 × 10⁻³ g/mL, i.e. 0.667 g/L); aqueous extract inhibited above 1 × 10⁻³ g/mL (IC50-4d 3.889 × 10⁻³ g/mL). Hydroxyethanesulfonic acid damaged PSII.
env_effects: Cells shrank and plasmolysed; photosystem II damaged.
key_details: Lab co-culture of an antibiotic-treated commercial N. closterium strain with G. bailiniae thalli collected from Fengjia Bay (Hainan), 22°C, salinity 30, 10 d, controls without seaweed, n = 3. Inhibition was dose-dependent with a significant concentration x time interaction (P < 0.01); the lowest extract dose (1 × 10⁻³ g/mL) was not inhibitory by day 10. Metabolomics identified citrate, hydroxyethanesulfonic acid and taurine as main intracellular compounds; HA damaged PSII (OEC, reaction centres). Target is a fouling diatom in seaweed aquaculture, not a toxic HAB species.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record duration '4 d' is the IC50 time point; experiments ran 10 d. Target is a benthic fouling diatom, not a bloom-forming HAB.

title: Kelp (Saccharina latissima) Mitigates Coastal Ocean Acidification and Increases the Growth of North Atlantic Bivalves in Lab Experiments and on an Oyster Farm
organism: sugar kelp (effect on water pH)
result: pH 7.44 → 7.74 / 8.01 / 8.42 at 0.3 / 0.7 / 1 g/L kelp; +0.15 pH inside field kelp lines.
env_effects: Kelp raised pH ~0.3-0.4 per day in a closed vessel, to ~8.8 by day 7.

title: Use of sugar kelp aquaculture in Long Island Sound and the Bronx River Estuary for nutrient extraction
organism: Saccharina latissima (sugar kelp) cultivation; nutrient bioextraction (no algae target)
scale: Two 50 m longlines per site at WLIS (Fairfield, CT) and CLIS (Branford, CT) and at the Bronx River Estuary mouth; N removal extrapolated to a hypothetical farm with 1.5 m longline spacing
dose: Kelp seedstrings outplanted on longlines at 0.5 and 1.0 m depth
duration: 2012-2013 winter-spring growing season (outplant late 2012 to harvest ~May-June 2013)
result: Estimated N removal up to 180 (BRE), 67 (WLIS) and 38 (CLIS) kg N/ha and C 1350/1800/1100 kg C/ha per season in a hypothetical farm; yield did not differ significantly among sites (p = 0.072), CLIS 62-69% of the others.
env_effects: Nitrogen removal co-benefit.
key_details: Field cultivation trial of native sugar kelp at three sites differing in temperature, salinity and nutrients (BRE >> WLIS ~ CLIS for DIN). Yield (kg FW per m longline) showed no depth effect (0.5 vs 1.0 m) and no significant site effect. N and C removal per hectare were extrapolated from tissue content and yield to a hypothetical 1.5 m-spaced farm; potential N-credit value up to $1600/ha (BRE). No phytoplankton, chlorophyll or HAB outcome was measured, so this is nutrient extraction only, one season, no replication across years.
fulltext_discrepancy: Per-hectare removals are model extrapolations to a hypothetical farm, not measured farm-scale removal; no HAB/algae endpoint.

title: Allelopathy in macroalgae: Ecological principles, research opportunities and pitfalls reviewed
organism: review of 138 allelopathic seaweeds
result: Lists confounders (nutrients, shading, contact, pH, bacteria); recommends a plastic mimic control; few studies held pH constant.
env_effects: Ulva intestinalis pushes rock pools above pH 10.
